extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for home health notice of admission (NOA) submissions.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. For home health agency claims:

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Humana does not require an NOA for home health services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Humana does not apply a reduction or penalty for a home health agency's failure to submit an NOA.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Humana denies an NOA as informational when received.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Humana applies consolidated billing for home health services. Humana does not reimburse separately for services that are part of home health packaged reimbursement, even when those services are billed separately.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Humana requires a provider to report a final claim with an accurate Health Insurance Prospective Payment System (HIPPS) code, as determined by the Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS), for each home health case.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. For home health agency claims:

Humana does not require an NOA for home health services.

Humana does not apply a reduction or penalty for a home health agency's failure to submit an NOA.

Humana denies an NOA as informational when received.

Humana applies consolidated billing for home health services. Humana does not reimburse separately for services that are part of home health packaged reimbursement, even when those services are billed separately.

Humana requires a provider to report a final claim with an accurate Health Insurance Prospective Payment System (HIPPS) code, as determined by the Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS), for each home health case.

Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting and reimbursement of Home Health Billing that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

Notice of admission (NOA): An NOA is a notice for the billing of home health agency claims. This submission is used by Original Medicare to open an episode of care.
